title: Chimney Rock marks the moon's 18.6-year standstill

tellings.quote: you peer through those through those two pinnacle rocks and it marks that position where you will see every 18.6 years you will see the moon rising in between those two rocks.

plain: A researcher named Randall Carlson, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, describes Chimney Rock in Colorado, where two tall rock pinnacles stand side by side. He says that if you look between them, they mark the exact spot where the moon rises once every 18.6 years, at the far end of its long cycle. If true, it would mean the people who once lived there were watching the sky carefully enough to track a cycle that takes nearly two decades.
